inspectionOrder: actual b176 native source collection linked in independent inspection scene
sourceObservations: Twelve long straight boards span the square dock, with narrow dark open joints, alternating four light boards and eight orange boards, eight tiny dark nail heads and two low underside joists.

Original top faces read as mostly flat orange bands, fine bevels produce only a narrow rim, and board ends are squared off. Long unbroken strips and tiny nails provide little crafted timber character.
The original remains a full 3x3 walking deck; no notch or entry-specific shape is visible in the original silhouette.
targetObservations: Target retains twelve long honey timber strips while making their upper corners and ends visibly round, softly inflated, and separated by deliberate dark seams.
Target timber has long flowing low-contrast grain, several elongated knots, varied golden versus amber strips and broad pale edge catches. Small domed charcoal fasteners have a readable silver glint.
The front edge shows substantial rounded timber thickness and small lower joist feet. Surface stays broad and useful, with detail subordinate to the deck.
styleObservations: Warm-soft reference uses warm saturated body color, broad rounded edge highlights, soft material transitions and a legible volume rather than flat unshaded panels.

Native adaptation should use real edge shaping and restrained directional grain material, with light evenly balanced between horizontal directions. No image halo or ground shadow is useful asset content.
implementationIntentBeforeCriteria: Rebuild native bevelled boards with broad rounded rims, procedural timber grain/knots, small sculpted nail heads and low joists while retaining fixed root, broad height and 3x3 role; measure source and transfer contract before modeling.
